issues.legal_issue: A prolonged delay in applying to substitute a deceased respondent in an appeal is not excused when the applicant had reason to know of the death and the circumstances do not adequately explain the delay.
material_facts: A respondent died while the appeal was pending, but the application to bring his legal representatives on record was filed several years later.
Even after excluding the time taken to obtain the High Court certificate, the application was delayed by about three and a half years.
The deceased was a prominent local resident, news of his death appeared in newspapers, and the applicant lived nearby.
The applicant had conducted the litigation for many years, remained in contact with her advocates, and had a son-in-law helping her.
The applicant relied on her poverty, illiteracy, lack of a male family member to manage the litigation, and the fact that the representatives had been added in later final decree proceedings.
issues.conclusion: There was no sufficient ground to excuse the delay in bringing the deceased respondent’s legal representatives on record in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XVI, rule 14 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1950, an application to bring a deceased respondent’s legal representatives on record must be made within the prescribed period, excluding time taken to obtain the High Court certificate. On the circumstances presented, the applicant’s asserted hardship did not sufficiently explain the substantial delay.

predicates.substitution_delay_application_in_appeal: The applicant sought to add a deceased respondent’s legal representatives to an appeal after the respondent died while the appeal was pending.
predicates.substantial_delay: The application was filed substantially beyond the prescribed time, even after excluding time taken to obtain a required certificate.
predicates.applicant_had_notice_of_death: The circumstances, including the public reporting of the death and the applicant’s proximity to the deceased, indicated that the applicant knew or could have learned of the death.
predicates.applicant_was_actively_conducting_litiga: The applicant had long conducted the litigation, maintained contact with legal representatives, and received assistance from a family member.

issues.definition: When a substitution-delay application in an appeal is substantially late and the applicant had notice of the death or was actively conducting the litigation with help, the delay is not excused.

issues.legal_issue: Adding a deceased party’s legal representatives in later proceedings in a suit does not preserve an appeal that had already been filed and in which the representatives were not added in time.
material_facts: A respondent died after an appeal against a preliminary decree had been filed.
The deceased respondent’s legal representatives were not brought on record in that appeal within the prescribed time.
The representatives were brought on record within time in later final decree proceedings in the suit.
The applicant argued that the final decree proceedings and the appeal were stages of the same suit, so the later substitution should prevent abatement of the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The order adding the legal representatives in the final decree proceedings did not benefit the previously filed appeal, which abated as against the deceased respondent.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII, rules 3, 4 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with Order XVI, rules 14 and 14-A of the Supreme Court Rules, 1950, treats a suit and an appeal as separate proceedings for abatement. An order adding legal representatives at one stage enures to subsequent stages, because an appeal is a continuation of the suit, but an order made in the suit after an appeal has already been filed cannot be projected backwards into that appeal. Brij Inder Singh v. Kanshi Ram, 44 I.A. 218, was distinguished; Shankarnaraina Saralaya v. Laxmi Hengsu, A.I.R. 1931 Mad. 277, was referred to.

predicates.appeal_pending_when_party_died: An appeal had already been filed and was pending when a party to it died.
predicates.representatives_not_added_to_appeal_in_t: The deceased party’s legal representatives were not brought on record in the appeal within the prescribed time.
predicates.representatives_added_in_later_suit_proc: The deceased party’s legal representatives were added in proceedings in the suit that occurred after the appeal had already been filed.

issues.definition: If a party dies while an appeal is pending, the representatives are not added to the appeal in time, and they are added only in later suit proceedings, the appeal abates as to that party.
